question: A 6-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department with difficulty in breathing. Her parents mention that the child has been experiencing an increasing difficulty in breathing over the past few weeks. It is more prominent when she plays outside in the garden. She has similar episodes about twice a week. She has had a slight difficulty in breathing in the past, but it used to subside once she was rested. During the last month, she has also woken up breathless a couple of times at night, the last episode having occurred last night. A pulmonologist suspects an intermittent obstructive lung disease and orders a pulmonary function test. Her forced expiratory volume is assessed before and after the administration of inhaled albuterol. Her readings are plotted in the graph below. Based on the graph below, which of the following percentage changes in her expiratory volumes would indicate a reversible obstructive pulmonary condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Child presents with difficulty in breathing" -> "Symptoms worsen with outdoor activity" -> "Episodes occur twice a week" -> "Nocturnal breathlessness noted" -> "Pulmonologist suspects intermittent obstructive lung disease" -> "Pulmonary function test ordered" -> "Forced expiratory volume assessed before and after albuterol" -> "Significant improvement in expiratory volume indicates reversibility" -> "Reversible obstructive pulmonary condition typically shows > -> 12%

CHAIN: "Child has history of respiratory issues" -> "Symptoms have increased in frequency and severity" -> "Pulmonary function test shows baseline expiratory volume" -> "Albuterol administered to assess reversibility" -> "Percentage change in expiratory volume calculated" -> "Reversible obstructive lung disease indicated by > -> 12%

CHAIN: "Child experiences episodic breathlessness" -> "Symptoms suggest possible asthma" -> "Pulmonary function test performed" -> "Albuterol used to evaluate response" -> "Improvement in expiratory volume indicates obstructive pattern" -> "Reversibility defined as > -> 12%
CHAIN: "Child's symptoms align with asthma diagnosis" -> "Pulmonary function test results expected to show improvement" -> "Albuterol is a bronchodilator" -> "Expected response is > -> 12%
analysis: In cases of reversible obstructive lung disease, such as asthma, a significant improvement in forced expiratory volume (FEV1) after bronchodilator administration is expected. A change of 12% or more is generally considered indicative of reversibility. Therefore, among the options provided, a percentage change of 12% would indicate a reversible obstructive pulmonary condition.
